text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government announced a slew of new measures aimed at cutting the waiting time for first-time applicants for Housing Board flats to about three years.
- A National Education Exhibition will be held next year to help foster better understanding for Singapore's past, present and future among adults, said Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong.
- Water rates for households will be raised progressively to drive home the message that water is precious and to make water conservation an ingrained habit among Singaporeans.

- Troubled Amcol Holdings reported a Singapore $340 million net loss after extraordinary items for the nine months ended September last year -- including a Singapore $68 million write-off on its controversial Mauritius venture and its Chinese power project.
- More people are buying travel insurance because of greater media publicity about Singaporeans getting hurt while travelling overseas, greater affluence, and a better-educated population.

- Thailand's commercial banks will set up a fund worth as much as 50 billion baht to bolster the country's share market, the world's worst performer in the past 18 months, Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said.

- Wall Street's market strategists and analysts expect Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan to disregard recent data suggesting a slowing economy and raise interest rates a quarter point at tomorrow's meeting of the Febd's policy making body.
- The government has taken decisive steps to cut the waiting time for first-time buyers and those in urgent need of HDB flats.
- The government looks set to proceed with building desalination plants to ensure a steady supply of water for Singapore.
- The government will soon announce a radical shift in the way it sets water tariffs, said Deputy Premier Lee Hsien Loong.
